recipes.name: The Ultimate Steak Sandwich
ingredients: 4 Fresno chiles (or jalapeños, serranos), thinly sliced
4 large shallots, peeled and sliced on a mandolin
1 cup grated gruyere, smoked gouda, or Comte cheese (or a mix of all)
instructions: For the Dry Brine

Dry brine the steak: generously coat all sides of the steak with salt and pepper - allow to rest at room temperature for 40 minutes to 2 hours (or overnight in the fridge). - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick - 1 tbsp kosher salt - 1 tsp freshly ground pepper
For the Toppings
Make the roasted garlic: Preheat oven to 400 F° Cut off the top of the head of garlic, exposing each clove - reserve cut-off garlic scraps. - 1 head of garlic
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and wrap tightly in aluminum foil. - olive oil divided - salt & pepper to taste - 1 head of garlic
Roast in the oven for 1 hour, until cloves are browned and jammy. - 1 head of garlic
For the Pickled Chiles
Combine chiles, sliced shallot, and reserved garlic clove scraps in a heat-proof bowl. - 4 Fresno chiles (or jalapeños serranos), thinly sliced - 1 shallot sliced
For the Pickling Liquid

In a medium saucepan, combine vinegar, water, salt, coriander seeds, mustard seeds, and honey - bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, then cook for 5 minutes, and tiny whisk until salt and honey are dissolved. - 1 cup apple cider vinegar - 1 cup water - 2 tbsp kosher salt - 1 tbsp coriander seeds - 1 tbsp mustard seeds - ⅓ cup honey
While the pickling liquid is cooking, prepare your shallots for frying - 4 large shallots peeled and sliced on a mandolin
Pour the pickling liquid over the chile mixture, mix then cover with a plate, and let rest for at least 20 minutes. - For the Pickling Liquid - For the Pickled Chiles
Drain and set aside (cover leftover chiles with pickling liquid and keep in the fridge for up to 2 weeks). - For the Pickled Chiles
For the Fried Shallots
Slice the shallots as uniformly as possible using a sharp knife or a mandolin. Then separate sliced shallots into their individual rings. - 4 large shallots peeled and sliced on a mandolin
Combine the sliced shallots and 1 cup vegetable oil in a cold, high-walled sauté pan. - 1 cup vegetable oil - 4 large shallots peeled and sliced on a mandolin
Heat over medium-high heat until bubbling, reduce heat and fry gently, stirring frequently, until golden-brown. - For the Fried Shallots

While the shallots are frying, optionally grate the cheeses, keeping an eye on the shallots and continuing to stir to ensure even frying. - 1 cup grated gruyere smoked gouda, or Comte cheese (or a mix of all)
Drain on paper towels (reserve shallot-infused oil for other recipes) and allow to cool. - For the Fried Shallots
For the Creamed Spinach
Prepare shallot and garlic by finely mincing. - 1 shallot finely minced - 1 clove garlic finely minced
In a large nonstick pan, heat butter over medium flame until foaming subsides. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Add shallot and sweat for 1-3 minutes, until just translucent. - 1 shallot finely minced
Add garlic and sauté for an additional 30 seconds, until fragrant. - 1 clove garlic finely minced
Add flour and mix with a rubber spatula until the vegetables are evenly coated. - 1 tbsp flour
Then, add half and half and mix, cooking for 1-2 minutes until the mixture begins to thicken. - 1 ½ cups half & half
Add freshly grated nutmeg and heat until the mixture comes to a simmer. - ½ tsp freshly grated nutmeg

Then, add the thawed spinach. Reduce heat to low, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, until very thick. (If fresh spinach, sauté first before adding to the cream) - 1 (10 oz) bag frozen spinach thawed

Optionally prepare steak and bread while the Creamed Spinach cooks, check on the pickled chiles, slice your bread loaf using the baking sheet method and a straight-edge knife, and remove the garlic from the oven. - For the Dry Brine - For the Pickled Chiles - 1 small pan cubano (or hoagie roll) - For the Roasted Garlic
Remove from heat, stir in parmigiano reggiano, season to taste with salt and pepper, cover and set aside. - 2 oz shredded parmigiano reggiano - salt & pepper to taste - For the Creamed Spinach
For the Steak
In a cast iron pan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat until smoking.
Increase heat to medium-high, press your dry-brined steak into the center of the pan, and weigh down with a heavy pan or chef weight. - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick
Cook for 3-5 minutes on the first side, until deeply and evenly browned, then flip. - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick
Cook for an additional 5-7 minutes, flipping as necessary, until rare (125 F° at its thickest point). - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick
Remove from the pan, cover with aluminum foil, and allow to rest for 10 minutes (residual heat will bring the temp up to medium-rare). - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick
For the Steak Sandwich Assembly
Scoop roasted garlic out of the skins. Slice Steak thinly, on a bias, across the grain. - For the Roasted Garlic - 1 boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick
Toast the bread in the reserved beef fat in the same cast iron pan (supplement with olive oil if there isn’t enough fat). - 1 small pan cubano (or hoagie roll)
Spread roasted garlic on both sides of the toasted bread. - head of garlic - 1 small pan cubano (or hoagie roll)
Spread Creamed Spinach on the bottom slice, top with Pickled Chiles, and shingle steak over top. - boneless ribeye (1.5 inch) thick - For the Creamed Spinach - For the Pickling Liquid

Top the steak with Fried Shallots, and press cheese over top - broil or torch until cheese is melted. Top with bread, press, slice in half, and enjoy. - For the Fried Shallots - 1 cup grated gruyere smoked gouda, or Comte cheese (or a mix of all)
